sourceLine: your San Luis Valley, San Antonio and reentry programs, and the questions educators ask before they scale VR career training

cards.title: Three Headsets, Six Counties, 260 Students
cards.angle: Transfr's March 2, 2026 San Luis Valley story reports three headsets reaching 260+ students across six counties and 8,000 square miles. Reach and hours logged are usage counts. The page says the headsets rotate among Monte Vista High School, Delta Center and a Boys & Girls Club.
cards.evidence: Your story reports 200+ sessions and 105 hours logged in total, and a 300+ student figure that is a projection. No article on your site explains the schedule, transport, maintenance and staffing behind that rotation.

sources.title: San Luis Valley Career-Connected Pathways Partnership

cards.title: Designing a Four-Day VR Career Lesson
cards.angle: San Antonio ISD reported 1,100+ students participating in Transfr sims, with 30 goggle sets bought this year after 8 earlier sets, per an April 29, 2026 republication of the district's story. The four-day sequence includes a 23-question interest inventory, and the stated goal is at least two sims per student.
cards.evidence: These are district-reported usage figures, not outcomes, and the page does not confirm that every student completed two sims. Your January 27, 2026 post covers how to start a career exploration program with VR. No article on your site explains how a teacher moves a class from an initial career choice to a useful discussion after the headset comes off.

cards.title: VR Reentry Training Needs Cohort Data
cards.angle: Transfr's August 19, 2026 post reports 17 graduates across two Leon County Detention Facility cohorts, 11 since released, after a 120-hour blended training program. That is not 120 hours of VR per learner. The 18 union recruits at Scott County Jail within six months are a separate facility-level result.
cards.evidence: Your post cites RAND recidivism figures second hand, says VR-specific longitudinal data is limited and calls the gap a research agenda, not a marketing problem. No article on your site specifies a follow-up design: which outcomes each partner tracks after release and for how long.
